metadata.title: GEEK Protocol — Kaspa integration reliability and encoding
metadata.schema: correctIndex is zero-based; options contains four distinct strings
metadata.reviewNotice: Internal source/wording/distractor review of the pinned Rusty Kaspa revision. Advanced integration material remains outside introductory Study. Implementation behavior does not establish universal wallet compatibility or network activation. Difficulty is provisional; independent editorial review is unassigned.
metadata.attribution: Original Geek Protocol questions based on pinned MIT-licensed Rusty Kaspa code; source prose and code are not imported.

questions.prompt: What problem does Rusty Kaspa's Resolver solve for an application without a fixed node URL?
options: Finding an available public wRPC endpoint
Confirming a transaction's acceptance without querying a node
Choosing the lowest fee for every future transaction
Providing the full node's consensus validation inside the browser
questions.funFact: The resolver discovers node endpoints. Discovery does not authorize spending or make a returned node an independent proof of ledger state.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which two caller choices are included in a Rusty Kaspa resolver request alongside its TLS preference?
options: Recipient address and transfer amount
Network ID and wRPC encoding
Transaction ID and output index
Account derivation depth and mnemonic word count
questions.funFact: The request path includes network_id and encoding, so discovery can select an endpoint for the intended network and wire format.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: When Rusty Kaspa's resolver first builds a request in an HTTPS browser context, which endpoint transport does it request?
options: Only unencrypted WebSocket transport
Only a local IPC transport
TLS-capable transport
The transport with the shortest URL regardless of encryption
questions.funFact: The browser branch recognizes HTTPS and selects the tls path. This avoids asking that secure page to use an insecure node connection.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: How can Rusty Kaspa's Resolver use an operator's own discovery services?
options: Pass node WebSocket URLs as mnemonic recovery words
Put the discovery-service URL in a transaction's payload
Change only the transaction's signature-hash mode
Supply a custom list of resolver URLs
questions.funFact: Custom URLs replace the bundled resolver-service list. Resolver services are distinct from the node endpoints that they return.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: How does Rusty Kaspa's resolver choose the order in which it tries its configured services?
options: It shuffles the list before trying services
It always picks the alphabetically first URL
It sorts services by their URL length
It always queries the bundled first service before any custom list
questions.funFact: Randomizing the attempt order distributes first attempts across services. The fetch loop returns when a service supplies a descriptor.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Every configured service fails in Rusty Kaspa's resolver fetch loop. What does the caller receive?
options: An empty descriptor presented as successful discovery
An error containing the collected failures
A guaranteed cached descriptor even if none was fetched
An automatic successful connection to localhost
questions.funFact: The loop collects service errors and returns failure after exhausting the list. An application must handle unavailable discovery explicitly.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: How do get_node and get_url differ in Rusty Kaspa's Resolver?
options: One queries mainnet only; the other queries testnet only
One discovers Borsh only; the other discovers JSON only
One returns a node descriptor; the other returns its URL string
One requires TLS; the other always disables TLS
questions.funFact: Both use the discovery fetch. get_url extracts the descriptor's URL, while get_node retains the descriptor information.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What URL behavior does Rusty Kaspa's KaspaRpcClient constructor documentation warn about?
options: A constructor URL is used only for the first connection
A constructor URL is ignored whenever a resolver is present
A constructor URL is automatically replaced after every RPC call
A constructor URL fixes the endpoint used by that client
questions.funFact: For an integration that needs to choose a URL on each connect call, the constructor documentation says to leave its URL argument as None.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What does Rusty Kaspa's KaspaRpcClient connect method do before starting its new connection attempt?
options: Disconnects the previous connection
Retains the old socket until the new connection has fully succeeded
Immediately declares the new endpoint synchronized
Reuses the old socket while changing only its displayed URL
questions.funFact: connect begins with disconnect, then acquires its connection guard and applies the new connection options.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What does the block option described for Rusty Kaspa's KaspaRpcClient connect operation wait for?
options: Completion of the node's entire synchronization process
The first successful connection
Acceptance of the next submitted transaction
Delivery of the first UTXO-change notification
questions.funFact: The documented option controls waiting for connection success. It is not a transaction confirmation or proof that a payment occurred.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: A Rusty Kaspa KaspaRpcClient connection fails under ConnectStrategy::Fallback. What cleanup does this branch perform?
options: Keeps those background services running in this error branch
Returns success with an empty RPC response
Shuts down the RPC client and stops background services
Retries without ever returning an error to the caller
questions.funFact: The fallback error branch explicitly shuts down the underlying client and stops services before returning the connection error.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Besides closing the endpoint connection, what does Rusty Kaspa's KaspaRpcClient disconnect method do?
options: Only clears the displayed URL while services keep running
Submits a replacement for every outgoing transaction
Stops the remote node's background consensus services
Stops its background RPC services
questions.funFact: disconnect calls the underlying shutdown and then stop. This is a client lifecycle operation, not an on-chain reversal.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What is the intended use of Rusty Kaspa's KaspaRpcClient trigger_abort helper?
options: Testing application reconnection behavior by aborting the socket
Requesting a graceful server shutdown
Canceling an already accepted transaction
Forcing an immediate successful reconnection
questions.funFact: The source marks trigger_abort as a debug facility for disrupting the underlying WebSocket and exercising recovery logic.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Rusty Kaspa's parse_url helper receives wss://node.example with no explicit port. How does it handle the default wRPC port?
options: Always appends the default Borsh port
Leaves the URL without an added port
Replaces the scheme with ws and adds the P2P port
Rejects the URL because its port was omitted
questions.funFact: An explicit scheme or path suppresses insertion of a default port when none was supplied, preserving reverse-proxy style endpoints.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: When Rusty Kaspa's parse_url helper needs a default port for a bare hostname, what determines that port?
options: Only the host operating system's default HTTP port
Only the address's public-key version
The selected network type and wRPC encoding
Only the first available local port
questions.funFact: The helper selects a network-specific Borsh or JSON RPC port. An explicitly provided port takes precedence.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Why does Rusty Kaspa's wallet scanner hold the processor's notification lock during a scan?
options: To prevent the node from adding any new blocks
To guarantee an immutable remote snapshot across the entire network
To prevent account address derivation from ever advancing
To coordinate the scan with concurrent notification processing
questions.funFact: The scan holds the guard across its address-manager or fixed-set scan. The processor's notification handler uses the corresponding write lock.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: How does EmptyWindow differ from Depth in Rusty Kaspa's wallet scanner's stopping policy?
options: It searches for an empty address range rather than a specified derivation depth
It scans exactly one address regardless of the result
It stops immediately after the first funded address
It chooses its stopping rule from the amount of transaction fees
questions.funFact: The extent selects a discovery stopping rule. A bounded-depth scan and an empty-window scan can inspect different ranges.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Why can the first range in Rusty Kaspa's address-manager scan exceed one ordinary window?
options: It always covers the complete u32 derivation space
It includes the known address index as well as the minimum window
It uses one address for every block in the DAG
It expands the range only when the node changes network
questions.funFact: The initial upper bound is the greater of last_address_index + 1 and window_size. Later ranges advance by the chosen window size.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which address-manager index does Rusty Kaspa's scan retain after discovering UTXOs at later derived addresses?
options: The first empty address after every completed scan
The highest index requested even if no UTXO was found there
The latest discovered used address index
Always the default window size regardless of discovered use
questions.funFact: The scan tracks the greatest matching derived index that returned UTXOs and writes it back to the address manager when scanning finishes.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What context does Rusty Kaspa's scanner use to classify each discovered UTXO's balance contribution?
options: Only the sum of output amounts without maturity classification
Only the number of addresses queried
Only the current transaction fee estimate
Network parameters and the current DAA score
questions.funFact: Each entry's balance calculation receives the selected network parameters and current score, rather than treating every discovered amount as mature.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which scan provider suits a caller that already has the exact Kaspa address set it wants to inspect?
options: AddressSet
AddressManager with an unbounded derivation extent
A list of block-template hashes
The connected node's peer-address table
questions.funFact: The scanner supports both derived address-manager ranges and a supplied fixed address set. The latter does not discover further derivation ranges.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: A Rusty Kaspa fixed-set scan finds UTXOs for several supplied addresses. How is its returned balance built?
options: By selecting only the largest discovered UTXO
By summing the classified contributions of the discovered entries
By multiplying the first address's balance by the set size
By treating every discovered output as immediately mature
questions.funFact: The fold accumulates mature and pending amounts and associated counts, then extends the context with the discovered UTXO references.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What separate condition does Rusty Kaspa's wallet SyncMonitor track beyond having a network connection?
options: Whether the socket has ever opened successfully
Whether the endpoint URL has a recognized scheme
Whether the connected node is synchronized
Whether a wallet has generated at least one address
questions.funFact: A reachable node can still be synchronizing. The monitor tracks node sync state and communicates it to the wallet.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Rusty Kaspa's SyncMonitor learns that its node is not synced and no monitoring task is running. What does it start?
options: An automatic outgoing-transaction rebroadcast
A new wallet address-range scan on every poll
A permanent Synced state until the socket disconnects
A background sync-monitor task
questions.funFact: track(false) marks the state unsynced, starts the task if needed and emits NotSynced. It does not authorize any payment.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: When Rusty Kaspa's SyncMonitor detects that the node has become synced, what wallet state does it report?
options: SyncState::Synced
Only the original NotSynced state until the wallet restarts
A transaction-specific acceptance guarantee
An automatic change of the wallet's configured network
questions.funFact: The synced transition updates the atomic state and notifies the wallet. A running monitor task can then stop rather than keep polling unnecessarily.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: How does Rusty Kaspa's source characterize its StateObserver that extracts sync stages from node stdout?
options: A consensus proof independent of log wording
A temporary log-parsing implementation
A stable wire protocol guaranteed across node releases
A replacement for node-reported synchronization status
questions.funFact: The comment explicitly describes temporary extraction from stdout pending a proper notification API. Integrators should scope such behavior to Rusty Kaspa's revision.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What happens during Rusty Kaspa's wallet processor's initialization if the server's RPC API version is newer than the client supports?
options: It assumes all newer APIs are backward compatible
It automatically upgrades the installed wallet code
Initialization returns an RPC API version error
It only changes the displayed version and continues
questions.funFact: The comparison rejects a newer server API version. This check does not claim that every differing revision or older version is incompatible.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Rusty Kaspa's wallet processor connects to a server without a UTXO index. How does initialization respond?
options: Reports a successful initialization with an assumed zero balance
Builds the missing remote index through this client call
Automatically changes to a random network with an index
Reports the missing index and returns an error
questions.funFact: The processor emits UtxoIndexNotEnabled and returns MissingUtxoIndex. Reachability alone is insufficient for this wallet workflow.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: A wallet configured for testnet-10 reaches a mainnet server in Rusty Kaspa's initialization flow. What happens?
options: Initialization rejects the network mismatch
It treats matching address payload sizes as enough to continue
It changes the expected network without notifying the caller
It accepts the server if the RPC API version matches
questions.funFact: The processor compares its expected network ID with the server-reported ID before accepting initialization.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Where does Rusty Kaspa's wallet processor obtain its initial current DAA score during server initialization?
options: The local machine's Unix timestamp
The server-info response's virtual_daa_score
The latest outgoing transaction's output index
The number of UTXOs returned by an address scan
questions.funFact: The server response supplies the virtual score, which is stored before normal wallet processing begins.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: If Rusty Kaspa's processor cannot negotiate its node connection, which behavior prevents silently continuing as initialized?
options: It silently assumes an empty wallet and continues
It reports successful initialization before retrying forever
It reports a processor error and disconnects the RPC client when available
It changes the configured network until negotiation succeeds
questions.funFact: The failed handle_connect branch notifies the application and attempts to disconnect the client, then returns the original error.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which local collections does Rusty Kaspa's wallet processor clear during disconnect cleanup?
options: The server's mempool and global UTXO index
The account's encrypted key storage and mnemonic
The remote node's blocks and peer database
Pending, stasis, outgoing and address-to-context tracking
questions.funFact: These are local tracking collections. Clearing them is lifecycle cleanup and does not erase or spend the underlying on-chain outputs.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Why does Rusty Kaspa's processor revisit pending and outgoing entries after a DAA-score change?
options: Their local lifecycle state can depend on score progression
Every score increase automatically confirms every pending entry
A score change replaces the account's public keys
Only a manual balance refresh can change entry maturity
questions.funFact: handle_daa_score_change stores and broadcasts the new score, then runs pending and outgoing processing.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Can a stasis entry move directly to the mature promotion list in Rusty Kaspa's processor when its assessed maturity is Confirmed?
options: No; an extra notification must always move it through pending
Yes; it need not be observed in pending first
No; confirmed stasis entries are always discarded
Only if the entry's amount exceeds the relay-fee threshold
questions.funFact: The stasis branch handles Confirmed by adding the entry to mature_entries and removing it from stasis. Pending is handled separately.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: The same address/outpoint appears in both added and removed UTXO lists in Rusty Kaspa's processor. How is it handled?
options: Counted once as a spend and once as unrelated new income
Ignored entirely, including any updated entry information
Separated as an update rather than an ordinary removal plus addition
Rejected as invalid without considering a context update
questions.funFact: The code extracts matching outpoints into common_added and later calls update_utxos, keeping this case distinct from genuine additions and removals.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: For the ordinary unmatched entries in a Rusty Kaspa UTXO-change batch, which pass runs first?
options: Additions, followed by ordinary removals
Only additions; the batch's removals are ignored
Only removals; the batch's additions are ignored
Removals, followed by additions
questions.funFact: After separating common outpoints, the processor handles remaining removed entries before the remaining added entries, then processes common updates.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: How does Rusty Kaspa's processor avoid refreshing the same affected context's balance once for every changed entry?
options: Collects affected contexts in a set, then updates each context
Refreshes every context once for every entry in the batch
Refreshes only the context containing the largest amount
Updates all account balances before applying the entry changes
questions.funFact: updated_contexts is a HashSet populated across the change passes. Balance refresh happens after processing those changes.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which notification scope does Rusty Kaspa's wallet processor start when registering its persistent listener?
options: Every block-template event
VirtualDaaScoreChanged
Only finality-conflict resolution events
A wildcard subscription to every address's UTXOs
questions.funFact: The listener registration starts virtual DAA-score notifications. Address tracking has its own UTXO subscription flow.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: In Rusty Kaspa's UTXO subscription mutation parser, what does Start with an empty address list mean?
options: Subscribe to no addresses
Subscribe only to addresses already present in this request
Subscribe to all addresses
Reject the request as missing a mandatory address
questions.funFact: An empty list is a wildcard for Start. A caller must not assume that an empty filter always means no event delivery.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: In Rusty Kaspa's UTXO subscription mutation parser, what does Stop with an empty address list request?
options: Remove only the first tracked address
Keep the existing subscription unchanged
Convert a selective subscription into a wildcard
Stop the entire UTXO subscription
questions.funFact: The parser maps an empty Stop scope to None, distinct from removing a specified nonempty set of addresses.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: An already selective Rusty Kaspa's UTXO subscription receives Start for more addresses. How does its selection change?
options: It becomes the union of the old and added address sets
It replaces the existing selection with only the new addresses
It retains only addresses shared by both sets
It removes the newly supplied addresses from the old selection
questions.funFact: The Selected plus Add branch registers additional addresses. Existing selected addresses remain in the selection.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: After a selective Rusty Kaspa's UTXO subscription removes its last tracked address, which state does it enter?
options: All, the wildcard state
None, the inactive state
Selected with an active but permanently empty filter
A new subscription containing the previously removed addresses
questions.funFact: The removal branch checks whether the tracked index set became empty and changes the subscription to None when it did.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: An All-state Rusty Kaspa's UTXO subscription receives Start for a specific nonempty address set. What is the resulting local selection?
options: All addresses except that set
All addresses with no local change
Only that selected address set
The intersection with an empty set, making it inactive
questions.funFact: This branch narrows the local state from All to Selected. Upstream mutations differ with AddressSet versus Wildcard policy.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: A Rusty Kaspa All-state UTXO subscription receives Stop for a specific nonempty address list. What does this branch do?
options: Creates an all-except-these exclusion filter
Stops the entire subscription regardless of the list
Replaces the wildcard with the listed addresses only
Leaves the All state unchanged
questions.funFact: The All plus Remove branch is a no-op. It does not implement a wildcard subscription with individual exclusions.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: When adding addresses to an already selective subscription, how do Rusty Kaspa's AddressSet and Wildcard policies differ upstream?
options: AddressSet forwards the new-address start; Wildcard needs no new upstream mutation
Both always restart the entire upstream subscription
Wildcard must send each newly added address separately
AddressSet never forwards additions while Wildcard always does
questions.funFact: The local selected set expands under either policy. An existing upstream wildcard already covers the additional addresses.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What happens when an already All-state Rusty Kaspa's UTXO subscription receives another wildcard Start?
options: Creates a second independent wildcard subscription state
No subscription change is produced
Converts the subscription into an empty selective state
Stops the current subscription before returning an error
questions.funFact: Repeated wildcard activation in the All state returns an empty mutation outcome, rather than creating another active subscription state.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What remains in a Rusty Kaspa active VirtualChainChanged notification when accepted transaction IDs are excluded?
options: An empty notification without either chain-hash list
Only removed hashes, with added hashes discarded
Added and removed chain hashes, with an empty accepted-ID list
Only added hashes, with removed hashes discarded
questions.funFact: The subscription filter preserves both chain-hash lists while replacing the accepted-ID list with an empty vector.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What does Rusty Kaspa's overall-notification filter return for an inactive subscription?
options: A copy of the full notification
An empty payload still marked as a delivered event
The most recent previously delivered notification
No delivered notification
questions.funFact: apply_overall_subscription returns None when inactive. Event filtering controls delivery, not the validity of the underlying chain event.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which score does Rusty Kaspa's SinkBlueScoreChanged event describe?
options: The virtual selected parent's blue score
The virtual state's DAA score
The number of blocks the local node has downloaded
The number of transactions in the latest template
questions.funFact: The event exposes sink_blue_score. It should not be confused with a player's XP or the separate virtual DAA-score event.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which Rusty Kaspa RPC event distinguishes resolution of a finality conflict from its initial report?
options: FinalityConflictCleared
FinalityConflictResolved
VirtualChainChanged
SinkBlueScoreChanged
questions.funFact: The RPC notification enum includes separate conflict and conflict-resolved variants, rather than representing resolution as a new payment.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which Rusty Kaspa RPC notification tells a mining integration that a new block template is available?
options: FinalityConflictResolved
SinkBlueScoreChanged
NewBlockTemplate
PruningPointUtxoSetOverride
questions.funFact: A mining client can react to template availability through this event. Availability alone does not mean that proof of work has been found.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Does successfully using Rusty Kaspa's ScriptBuilder establish that the resulting script will execute correctly?
options: Yes; successful construction proves all signatures valid
Yes; every canonically encoded script must evaluate true
Yes; the builder proves the referenced UTXOs exist
No; construction checks do not prove execution success
questions.funFact: The builder helps encode opcodes, integers and data within limits. Actual script semantics and spending validation remain separate checks.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: An add_op call would exceed Rusty Kaspa's builder's maximum script size. What happens to that attempted append?
options: It returns an error without appending the opcode
It truncates the existing script to make space
It appends the opcode but marks the result invalid afterward
It replaces the final existing opcode with the new opcode
questions.funFact: The limit check runs before script.push. A rejected append does not become a partially added opcode.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Why can add_data encode a single-byte small positive integer as one opcode in Rusty Kaspa's builder?
options: It always emits a four-byte length prefix
It selects the corresponding canonical small-integer opcode
It strips the value and emits an empty-vector push
It stores every integer as an eight-byte two's-complement word
questions.funFact: The builder recognizes the small-integer range and Op1Negate representation, reducing the encoding instead of always emitting a length plus data.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: When should a Rusty Kaspa builder caller consider add_data_with_push_opcode instead of add_data?
options: When the caller wants to bypass element-size checks
When the caller wants the builder to execute the script
When an explicit data-push form is needed without small-integer canonicalization
When the caller wants every data value converted to an integer opcode
questions.funFact: The explicit method chooses the push prefix from payload length and still validates the data push. It does not replace small integers with their integer opcodes.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Why can a data append fail in Rusty Kaspa's builder even if the whole script would fit its total length limit?
options: Every data element must have exactly eight bytes
Only the first element may contain nonzero bytes
Every data append requires a valid transaction signature
The individual element can exceed its own size limit
questions.funFact: validate_data_push checks both total encoded script size and the separate maximum element length.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which byte order does Rusty Kaspa's builder use for multi-byte OpPushData2 and OpPushData4 length prefixes?
options: Little-endian
Big-endian
Host-native order without conversion
Decimal text followed by a colon
questions.funFact: The builder explicitly serializes u16 and u32 data lengths with to_le_bytes before appending the actual payload bytes.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What does drain do to Rusty Kaspa's builder's accumulated script bytes?
options: Returns a copy while retaining all accumulated bytes
Returns them and leaves an empty internal vector
Returns only the last appended opcode
Returns the script hash while retaining the script internally
questions.funFact: drain takes ownership of the vector through mem::take. The source notes that the builder is not intended to retain its prior capacity for reuse afterward.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: How does Rusty Kaspa's script integer serializer represent a negative integer's sign?
options: A UTF-8 minus sign before decimal digits
A fixed two's-complement eight-byte word
A sign bit in the final magnitude byte
A separate leading byte that is always 0xff
questions.funFact: serialize_i64 emits magnitude bytes and sets the high bit of the last byte for negatives. This is signed-magnitude script encoding.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Why can Rusty Kaspa's script integer serializer append a zero byte to a positive magnitude?
options: To force every integer to use exactly eight bytes
To distinguish a transaction input from an output
To store the address network prefix beside the number
To keep its high magnitude bit from being interpreted as a negative sign
questions.funFact: When the highest magnitude byte has its high bit set, the serializer adds a sign-protection byte. The added byte is part of the integer encoding.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What integer does Rusty Kaspa's deserialize_i64 helper return for an empty byte vector?
options: Zero
Negative one
The maximum signed 64-bit value
